Thanks again for the pilot walkthrough last week. As we head into Q4 planning, our finance and product teams want a clearer view of how different tier and feature mixes would impact our spend and feature availability if we move from Pilot -> Growth -> Enterprise across the next 12 months.

Connor — I ran three quick scenario sweeps and put notes in the shared drive. High-level summary below; workbook attached (sim-results-connor-v1.xlsx). Link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/clearpoint/tier-rebalance-sims

Summary (short):
- Conservative (baseline growth +5% MoM seats, modest throughput): ~+18% ARR impact vs pilot baseline, most savings come from enabling KV cache sharing and modest batching (no quality change).
- Aggressive (seats +20% MoM, heavy streaming): ~+46% ARR impact; to keep latency under 350ms at peak you'll need dedicated burst capacity or quantized variants for non-critical routes. Quantization saves ~22% CPU/GPU costs but increases rerank variance slightly; recommend A/B on low-risk routes first.
- Compressed fallback (keep features most customers need): by gating: (1) advanced reranking, (2) long-term KV retention, (3) heavy-function calling. This reduces bill ~28% but causes feature gaps for two internal endpoints. We mapped the endpoints to feature impact in the workbook.

Playbook recommendations (one-paragraph each):
1) Step-up path: Pilot -> Growth (90-day check, enable shared KV and soft batching) -> Enterprise (commit + dedicated pool once 60% utilization sustained).
2) Fallback path: temporarily gate advanced reranking + reduce KV retention to 7 days; provide monitoring alerts and an auto-fallback toggle.
3) Pricing anchor/credit: propose a 10% usage credit in the first quarter post-upgrade tied to stability KPIs.

I included quick sensitivity charts and a recommended email to procurement in the Drive doc. If you want, Lauren can help tighten the anchor language.

—Ben
(attachment: sim-results-connor-v1.xlsx, XLSX, 460KB)
